THE USER'S REQUEST: "Make this model better at math. We use it with thinking mode on to solve competition-style math problems: the user message is the problem followed by "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}." Example problems of the kind we use, with reference answers, are in examples.jsonl."
Your adapter will be judged on held-out competition math problems of this kind (is the final \boxed{} answer correct), with thinking mode on, sampling at temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, presence penalty 1.5, and up to 32,768 new tokens per problem, and on not damaging the model's other abilities.

MODEL. Qwen3.5-0.8B (text part): 24 decoder layers of width 1,024. Layers 3, 7, 11, 15, 19 and 23 are full (gated) softmax attention (self_attn.q/k/v/o_proj, o_proj 1024 x 2048); the other 18 are linear attention (Gated DeltaNet: linear_attn.in_proj_*, a short convolution, an internal gated norm, linear_attn.out_proj 1024 x 2048). SwiGLU MLPs of width 3,584 (mlp.gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj 1024 x 3584). PRE-NORM: input_layernorm before attention and post_attention_layernorm before the MLP; sublayer outputs are added to the residual stream directly (no norm on the outputs). Final model.norm and a tied 248,320-token embedding.
Weights (bf16, safetensors, read-only): /workspace/model/model.safetensors-00001-of-00001.safetensors. A linear module computes y = W x with W of shape (d_out, d_in).
Thinking mode is on by default for this use; the tools let you choose.

YOUR WORKSPACE: /workspace/work. Tool outputs are written there (gen/<k>.json, acts/...). Examples from the user: examples.jsonl.
Use your own shell and Python in this sandbox to analyze files (numpy, scipy and safetensors are installed; there is no torch and no GPU).

HOW TO WORK. Nobody gives you a benchmark or a diagnosis. Write your own tests, look at what the model actually does
(generate, then check its answers), find what goes wrong and why, decide what a weight edit can fix, and write the adapter. Keep some of
your own tests aside to check your reasoning.

WHAT YOU CONTROL. A LoRA update dW = B @ A (rank r <= 8, ||dW|| <= 5.0 x ||W||) on any subset of the
writable modules: for each layer i = 0..23, mlp.down_proj (1024 x 3584) and the attention output projection: model.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj for i in {3,7,11,15,19,23}, model.layers.{i}.linear_attn.out_proj otherwise (both 1024 x 2048). Use module names model.layers.{i}... in the adapter; in model.safetensors the same weights are stored under model.language_model.layers.{i}...weight.
Adapter file: an .npz in your workspace with keys '<module>::A' (r x d_in) and '<module>::B' (d_out x r).

MODEL TOOLS (the only way to run the model; budgets are fixed):
- generate: <= 25 calls of <= 32 prompts, <= 16384 new tokens, decoding: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, presence-penalty 1.5. Can
  continue from a reply prefix (resample from any point of a reply).
- Analysis of the unedited model, <= 50 calls in total: inspect, inspect_module_inputs (last token),
  trace (activations at any positions or spans of any text, including the model's own replies), token_stats
  (per-token log-prob and entropy of a reply), logit_lens, attribution (each block's direct contribution to target
  logits), attention (full-attention layers), top_activations (where a neuron or direction fires in your texts),
  patch (copy activations from one text into another).
  Texts are items {user, reply, gen_ref}: gen_ref "gen/3.json:5" reuses saved generation 5 of gen/3.json.
  Sites: resid.L (residual stream entering layer L; resid.24 = after the last layer, before the final norm),
  a module name under model.layers (its input, e.g. model.layers.15.mlp.down_proj = the MLP neurons), or
  <module>:out (its output). Positions index the reply (0 = first reply token; -1 = last token).
- commit_adapter (once; ends the session).

RULES (Track A, one-shot):
- You may inspect the UNEDITED model only: weights (your own code), behavior (generate with adapter='') and

- Do not evaluate an edited model in any way (no generation with your adapter, no re-implementation of the network to

- No gradient descent, autograd, optimizers or iterative fitting of weights to a loss. Do not install packages.
- Commit exactly one adapter with commit_adapter. You will not see its score.

import json,struct,numpy as np
PATH='/workspace/model/model.safetensors-00001-of-00001.safetensors'
with open(PATH,'rb') as f:
 n=struct.unpack('<Q',f.read(8))[0]; header=json.loads(f.read(n))
START=8+n

def weight(key):
 h=header[key]; a,b=h['data_offsets']; dt=h['dtype']
 if dt=='BF16':
  m=np.memmap(PATH,mode='r',offset=START+a,dtype=np.uint16,shape=tuple(h['shape']))
  return (m.astype(np.uint32)<<16).view(np.float32)
 return np.array(np.memmap(PATH,mode='r',offset=START+a,dtype={'F32':np.float32,'F16':np.float16}[dt],shape=tuple(h['shape'])),dtype=np.float32)

def key_for(mod): return mod.replace('model.layers.','model.language_model.layers.')+'.weight'
if __name__=='__main__':
 from scipy.sparse.linalg import svds
 import os
 os.makedirs('weight_analysis',exist_ok=True)
 results={}
 for l in range(24):
  for part in ['mlp.down_proj','self_attn.o_proj' if l%4==3 else 'linear_attn.out_proj']:
   mod=f'model.layers.{l}.{part}'; w=weight(key_for(mod))
   u,s,v=svds(w,k=8,which='LM',random_state=42); ix=np.argsort(s)[::-1];u=u[:,ix];s=s[ix];v=v[ix]
   np.savez(f'weight_analysis/L{l}_{part}.npz',u=u,s=s,v=v)
   row=dict(norm=float(np.linalg.norm(w)),max=float(np.max(np.abs(w))),top=s.tolist())
   results[mod]=row
   print(mod,'frob',round(row['norm'],3),'max',round(row['max'],3),'S',np.round(s,3),flush=True)
 json.dump(results,open('weight_analysis/summary.json','w'),indent=2)
 print('other layer weight norms')
 for k,h in header.items():
  if 'language_model.layers.' in k and k.endswith('weight') and any(a in k for a in ['layernorm','mlp.gate_proj','mlp.up_proj']):
   w=weight(k);print(k,round(float(np.linalg.norm(w)),3),round(float(np.max(np.abs(w))),3))

"""One-shot, no-gradient construction. This script performs no model inference."""
import json,collections,numpy as np
from weights import weight,key_for
from mode_analysis import erows,g
from tokenize_local import vocab,encode,decode

MODULE='model.layers.22.mlp.down_proj'
GAIN=1.2
# Original-model matched-context difference, with common nonthinking directions removed.
u=np.load('acts/reconsideration_input.npy').astype(np.float64)
u/=np.linalg.norm(u)

# Protect common language/math readouts, ordinary termination, and code delimiters.
# All frequencies are from frozen-model replies, not target answers.
freq=collections.Counter()
for k in range(5):
 for item in json.load(open(f'gen/{k}.json')):
  freq.update(encode(item['reply']))
end_id=vocab['</think>']
protected={i for i,_ in freq.most_common(128) if i!=end_id}
for text in ['<|im_end|>','<|endoftext|>','<think>','Wait',' Wait','wait',' wait',
             'No',' No','Let',' Let','So','Therefore','The','However',
             '\n','\n\n','```',' ```','`',' ', '   ',
             '0123456789','+-=*/^()[]{}',r'\boxed{}',r'\frac',r'\sqrt']:
 protected.update(encode(text))
protected.discard(end_id)
protected=sorted(protected)
E=(erows(protected)*g).astype(np.float64)
end=(erows([end_id])[0]*g).astype(np.float64)
# Orthogonal projection is a closed-form geometric constraint, not loss fitting.
_,s,vh=np.linalg.svd(E,full_matrices=False)
Q=vh[s>1e-9*s[0]].T
b=end-Q@(Q.T@end)
retained=float(np.linalg.norm(b)/np.linalg.norm(end))
b*=GAIN/float(end@b)
A=u[None,:].astype(np.float32)
B=b[:,None].astype(np.float32)
assert A.shape==(1,3584) and B.shape==(1024,1)
assert np.isfinite(A).all() and np.isfinite(B).all()
w=weight(key_for(MODULE))
delta_norm=float(np.linalg.norm(A)*np.linalg.norm(B))
original_frob=float(np.linalg.norm(w))
original_spectral=float(np.load('weight_analysis/L22_mlp.down_proj.npz')['s'][0])
assert delta_norm <= 5*original_frob
assert delta_norm <= 5*original_spectral
path='/workspace/work/math_completion_adapter.npz'
np.savez(path,**{MODULE+'::A':A,MODULE+'::B':B})
meta={
 'path':path,'module':MODULE,'rank':1,'gain':GAIN,
 'A_shape':list(A.shape),'B_shape':list(B.shape),
 'update_frobenius_and_spectral_norm':delta_norm,
 'original_frobenius_norm':original_frob,
 'original_spectral_norm':original_spectral,
 'relative_frobenius_norm':delta_norm/original_frob,
 'relative_spectral_norm':delta_norm/original_spectral,
 'protected_readout_count':len(protected),'protected_subspace_rank':Q.shape[1],
 'end_direction_retained_fraction':retained,
 'protected_readout_max_abs_inner_product':float(np.max(np.abs(E@B[:,0]))),
 'end_readout_inner_product':float(end@B[:,0]),
 'construction':'Matched original thinking/nonthinking MLP-input contrast; remove control mean and 16 principal directions; rank-one end-of-thought readout with common-token null constraints.',
 'edited_model_evaluated':False,'gradients_or_training_used':False,
 'protected_token_ids':protected,
}
json.dump(meta,open('adapter_metadata.json','w'),indent=2)
print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in meta.items() if k!='protected_token_ids'},indent=2))
# Validate the serialized artifact, not model behavior.
with np.load(path,allow_pickle=False) as z:
 assert sorted(z.files)==sorted([MODULE+'::A',MODULE+'::B'])
 assert np.array_equal(z[MODULE+'::A'],A)
 assert np.array_equal(z[MODULE+'::B'],B)
print('Artifact validation passed.')
PY
